questions.label: Topic
questions.prompt: What do you want to study? Be specific about the question, what's known, and what success looks like.
questions.placeholder: e.g. Compare three numerical integrators on a damped harmonic oscillator and report energy drift.

questions.label: What is the result for?
questions.prompt: Research or a decision gets every check the result needs before it can be trusted; exploring is a cheaper, preliminary draft.

choices.label: Research (default)
choices.description: Checked the way a study must be before its result can be trusted: the plan waits for you to read it, every check stops the quest instead of only reporting, the experiment runs in its own clean environment, and four reviewers (method, statistics, reproducibility, devil's advocate) read the paper. Slower, and it stops for you more often.

choices.label: A decision
choices.description: The same checks as Research: a result someone will act on needs every one of them.

choices.label: Exploring (cheaper draft)
choices.description: A quick look: fewer model calls (no self-critique of the ideas, no per-finding cross-check, no redesign after the analysis), and the result is a preliminary draft, never ready to publish as it stands.

questions.label: Paper format / venue
questions.prompt: Picks the LaTeX template + writing persona. 'generic' is safe for scientific topics; 'essay' for non-computational humanities/social-science.

choices.label: generic — scientific paper, IMRAD
choices.description: Default for scientific topics. Surveys, comparative reviews, theoretical derivations, brief preprints.

choices.label: NeurIPS — ML benchmark / algorithm
choices.description: Empirical ML, neural networks, learning algorithms, journal-length.

choices.label: ICLR — representation learning
choices.description: Representations, generative models, ML theory.

choices.label: IEEE Access — engineering / systems
choices.description: Hardware/software architectures, measurement studies, engineering experiments. Two-column layout.

choices.label: Nature MI — physical sciences
choices.description: Physics / chemistry / materials simulation, scientific-method experiments.

choices.label: essay — long-form argumentative prose
choices.description: Cultural / historical / intellectual / qualitative cross-case analysis. Argue a thesis.

choices.label: report — consulting-style exec report
choices.description: Business / operational / market analysis with cover + TOC. Decision-maker audience.

choices.label: policy brief — 2-4 page recommendation
choices.description: Single decision for policymakers. Issue + context + recommendation.

choices.label: whitepaper — 8-20 page industry analysis
choices.description: Vendor-neutral tech trends / standards / architecture comparisons. Practitioner audience.

questions.label: Outputs
questions.prompt: Which deliverables matter? PDF gracefully degrades to MD if pandoc isn't installed.

choices.label: paper + PDF (recommended)
choices.description: Markdown + rendered PDF; needs pandoc + LaTeX on PATH. Falls back to MD-only when missing.

choices.label: everything
choices.description: paper, PDF, slides, poster, talk script. Maximum tooling needed (pandoc + LaTeX + marp + Beamer).

choices.label: paper + PDF + slides
choices.description: PDF via pandoc + LaTeX; slides via Marp; .pptx via pandoc.

choices.label: paper only (Markdown)
choices.description: Fastest path; no extra system tools needed.

questions.label: Paper style
questions.prompt: How should paper.pdf look? 'latex' is the classic Computer Modern article; 'briefing' is the Frontier Insight brand look (warm paper + teal, matching the slides/poster) rendered without LaTeX.

choices.label: LaTeX — Computer Modern article (default)
choices.description: The classic typeset look via the venue LaTeX template. Best typography; needs a LaTeX engine (or the HTML fallback).

choices.label: Briefing — Frontier Insight brand look
choices.description: Warm paper, deep-teal accents, serif display + brand mark — the same identity as the slides and poster. Rendered via pandoc + a browser (no LaTeX); single-column regardless of venue.

questions.label: Poster size
questions.prompt: Sheet size for poster.pdf. Text meets the poster font-size standards at every size; a bigger sheet holds more words.

choices.label: A1 portrait — 59.4 × 84.1 cm (default)
choices.description: Two columns. The usual conference poster size outside North America.

choices.label: A0 portrait — 84.1 × 118.9 cm
choices.description: Two columns on a larger sheet, so it holds more words.

choices.label: 48 × 36 in landscape — 121.9 × 91.4 cm
choices.description: Three columns. A common size at North American conferences.

questions.label: Study depth
questions.prompt: How mature should the resulting paper be? Drives word count + citation depth.

choices.label: brief preprint
choices.description: 1–2 pages, terse opening, focus on novel findings only. Citations OK to be few.

choices.label: journal-length (recommended)
choices.description: 4–8 pages with full IMRAD (or prose equivalent). ~15 citations, 1500–2500 words.

choices.label: comprehensive review
choices.description: 10–15 pages with Background + Comparison + Synthesis sections. 4000+ words, 10+ discussed citations.

questions.label: LLM provider
questions.prompt: Which transport for LLM calls. VSCode pins this to vscode_extension automatically.

choices.label: openai — HTTP direct (OpenAI API)
choices.description: Needs OPENAI_API_KEY. Fastest path, billed against your OpenAI account.

choices.label: codex — HTTP direct (ChatGPT Plus/Pro OAuth backend)
choices.description: Same transport as openai, points at ChatGPT's backend. Needs OPENAI_API_KEY.

choices.label: claude_cli — local Claude Code CLI
choices.description: Needs `claude` binary on PATH + `claude login`. Uses your Claude Pro/Max OAuth.

choices.label: codex_cli — local Codex CLI
choices.description: Needs `codex` binary on PATH + `codex login`. Uses your ChatGPT Plus/Pro OAuth.

choices.label: copilot_cli — local GitHub Copilot CLI
choices.description: Needs `gh` + Copilot Pro/Business. Uses `gh auth login`.

choices.label: gemini_cli — local Gemini CLI
choices.description: Needs `gemini` binary on PATH. Uses Google AI Studio OAuth.

choices.label: ollama — local server
choices.description: Needs Ollama running. Free, fully local; smaller models.

questions.label: Provider model
questions.prompt: Which model to call. Curated list per provider; pick 'Other' to type a model name not yet on the list.

questions.label: Title (short slug)
questions.prompt: Short identifier for this quest. Used in folder names. Auto-slugged from your topic; edit if you want something different.

questions.label: Research approach
questions.prompt: Decides whether the engine runs a Python experiment or waits for real-world data. Auto-derived from paper format.

choices.label: Computational — a Python script can produce the data
choices.description: Run normal implement → execute pipeline. For physics / ML / algorithmic / benchmark topics.

choices.label: Observational — needs real-world data the engine can't simulate
choices.description: Skip implement / execute; route to wait_for_data + auto_collect_data. For cultural / historical / qualitative / policy topics.

questions.label: Literature synthesis (survey) mode
questions.prompt: Is this a pure literature / history synthesis (a history, overview, or evolution of a subject) with NO experiment and NO dataset? If yes, the engine skips both and writes a descriptive synthesis. Auto-suggested for history/overview topics.

choices.label: No — run an experiment or analyse data (default)
choices.description: Normal pipeline: the engine designs an experiment (or, for observational topics, analyses collected data).

choices.label: Yes — a literature / history synthesis, no experiment or data
choices.description: Skip BOTH the experiment AND the dataset. The paper is a descriptive history / overview synthesised from the cited sources, with license-clean illustrative images. For 'history of X' / 'evolution of X' / overview topics. Implies observational.

questions.label: Pre-flight clarification mode
questions.prompt: Whether the engine pauses to confirm clarify slots. Pinned interview answers win regardless.

choices.label: Agent self-clarifies (recommended)
choices.description: Agent generates the questionnaire AND auto-answers it from the topic. Pinned interview answers still win.

choices.label: Pause for me to answer
choices.description: Engine pauses; you confirm/edit each clarify slot. Highest quality, most interruption.

choices.label: Just run it
choices.description: Skip the clarify node entirely. Engine relies on the interview answers + topic alone.

questions.label: Reviewer panel
questions.prompt: Recommended: 3-persona panel — the methodologist is the must-flag-rule reviewer; dropping the panel loses those checks. Single-reviewer is cheaper but ships without the non-bypassable design-quality enforcement.

choices.label: 3-persona panel (default)
choices.description: Methodologist + Statistician + Devil's-advocate + moderator. ~4× the review cost. Methodologist is the must-flag-rule reviewer — drop the panel and you lose those checks.

choices.label: Single reviewer (cheapest, no must-flag enforcement)
choices.description: 1 LLM call per review pass. Loses the methodologist must-flag rules.

choices.label: 4-persona panel
choices.description: Adds Reproducibility reviewer (seeds, raw data, the protocol; worth it for a stochastic simulation study). ~5× the review cost.

questions.label: Pause for user-supplied papers / datasets
questions.prompt: Pause mid-quest so you can drop reference PDFs into inputs/papers/ and datasets into inputs/data/ before the engine continues. After-literature stops once the literature is saved, so the experiment is designed with it in hand; after-design lets you correct the methodology; after-paper lets you augment the first draft. Resume with `fi --resume <quest_id>`.

choices.label: Never (default)
choices.description: Engine runs to completion without pause-drop opportunities.

choices.label: Pause after literature
choices.description: Stop once the literature is saved; skills, design and the experiment start on resume with it in hand (the search is not run again).

choices.label: Pause after design
choices.description: Drop reference papers / data BEFORE the implement → execute → analyze stages spend compute.

choices.label: Pause after paper draft
choices.description: Drop reference papers / data AFTER the first paper.md is written; useful for revise iterations.

choices.label: Both
choices.description: Pause after design AND after paper — most cost. Use for high-stakes manual review.

questions.label: Knowledge layer (Axon)
questions.prompt: Auto-detected from the Axon sidecar status. Override only if you have a specific reason.

choices.label: Disabled — turns OFF all retrieval
choices.description: Master switch: no Axon, no academic search (arXiv/OpenAlex/Crossref), and no web search. The quest runs on the model's own knowledge only.

choices.label: Enabled (recommended)
choices.description: Turns retrieval ON. Axon is used as the corpus only if installed — academic + web search work either way, so enable this even without Axon.

questions.label: Web research
questions.prompt: Search the public web for current sources and download them into the quest's data/literature/ folder. Runs for simulation AND observational quests, on top of academic retrieval. Does NOT require Axon, but it does require the knowledge layer above to be Enabled — that setting is the master switch for all retrieval.

choices.label: On (recommended)
choices.description: Search the public web (Brave / DuckDuckGo) for current sources and download them into the quest's data/literature/ folder — for BOTH simulation and observational quests. Adds real-world reports / news on top of academic retrieval.

choices.label: Off
choices.description: Skip the general web layer; rely on academic sources (and Axon, if enabled) only. No web pages are searched or downloaded.

questions.label: Paper audience
questions.prompt: External-facing (journal, open web) drops FI-internal cross-quest entries from the References; internal-facing keeps everything (good for project reports, memos, onboarding docs).

choices.label: External — journal / open web (recommended)
choices.description: FI's own cross-quest memory (fi_critique / fi_digest / fi_portfolio / fi_proposal / fi_summary) is dropped from References; an outside reader can't look those up. Real external sources + your own ingested papers are kept.

choices.label: Internal — team report / memo / onboarding
choices.description: Cite anything in Axon, including FI's own cross-quest summaries. Use for write-ups your team will read.

questions.label: Supply paywalled papers
questions.prompt: When a relevant paper is paywalled (SPIE / IEEE / Elsevier …) and only its abstract is reachable, pause and list the papers to download (ranked, with links) so you can drop the PDFs into inputs/papers/ and resume with real full text. On by default.

choices.label: Off
choices.description: Use whatever the open-web / open-access fetch can get. Paywalled papers (SPIE, IEEE, …) are cited by their abstract only. Choose this for an unattended run.

choices.label: Pause for my PDFs (default)
choices.description: When the agent can only get the abstract of a relevant paper, it pauses and writes a ranked needs/WANTED_PAPERS.md (download links + why each matters). Drop the PDFs into inputs/papers/ and resume — they're ingested as full text. Tip: you can also pre-load a folder of papers via knowledge.local_papers.

questions.label: Stop to read and edit the plan
questions.prompt: Every quest writes its plan (plan.md: what the literature says, the gap, the design the experiment will run) after the literature and before the experiment is designed. Stop there to read it and edit it, or ask for a change, before any compute is spent.

choices.label: Don't stop (default)
choices.description: The plan is written to plan.md in the quest folder, and the experiment is designed from it, but the quest does not wait. Choose this for an unattended run.

choices.label: Stop to read and edit the plan
choices.description: After the literature is in, the quest writes plan.md (what the literature says, the gap, the design) and stops. Edit the file, or ask for a change (--revise-plan, the quest page's Plan box, @fi /plan), then resume: the design block in the file is what runs.

questions.label: Comparative baseline
questions.prompt: What existing method / dataset / regime should this study be compared against? Topic-tuned default suggested by the preflight clarify call.
questions.placeholder: e.g. RandomForest baseline on the same features

questions.label: Success metric
questions.prompt: What number changing in what direction = headline result?
questions.placeholder: e.g. AUC ≥ 0.9 on held-out test set

questions.label: Time / compute budget
questions.prompt: Soft cap on wall-clock for the experiment.
questions.placeholder: e.g. a few minutes on a laptop CPU

questions.label: Axon hits per quest
questions.prompt: Dense-embedding retrievals from Axon fed to the writer. Small-k is precision (8 default); bump to 12-15 for comprehensive reviews. External web hits are sized separately via 'External hits per quest'.

questions.label: External hits per quest
questions.prompt: arXiv / OpenAlex / Crossref / S2 results when Axon misses. Bigger than Axon's cap because web search is coarser and a literature scan needs breadth. 20 default; 30+ for survey-shaped quests.

questions.label: Multi-model ensemble
questions.prompt: Run the same node across multiple LLMs and merge their answers. Cost multiplies; agreement signal increases. Pick 'off' for single-model (cheapest) or one of the fan-out profiles for higher-stakes work.

choices.label: Single model (default, cheapest)
choices.description: One LLM call per node. Cost baseline = 1×.

choices.label: Fan out cross_check only (~1.3× cost)
choices.description: 3 models vote per finding; catches issues the writer might miss. Minimal extra spend.

choices.label: Fan out ideate + cross_check (~2.0× cost)
choices.description: 3 models brainstorm + moderator picks the strongest; 3 models vote on each finding.

choices.label: Fan out ideate + analyze + cross_check (~2.5× cost)
choices.description: Multi-model on the three highest-leverage nodes. Best signal; highest cost.

questions.label: Models for the ensemble
questions.prompt: Only when you picked a fan-out profile above: the models to fan out over, one id per model, comma separated (at least 2). FI does not choose them for you — which models are worth the cost, and which you have access to, is your call. Leave empty and no ensemble is configured.

questions.label: Design-revise iteration budget
questions.prompt: Hard cap on the design → review → revise loop (and the cross_check redirects to design / literature). Lower = cheaper + faster; higher = more chances to fix issues review caught. 2 default — bump to 3-4 only when you specifically want extra revise passes.

questions.label: Per-node model overrides
questions.prompt: Route specific nodes to a different model than the primary one, e.g. a cheaper model for the light nodes. Measured on one simulation topic (3 runs each), moving cross_check, select_skills, literature_screen, slides and poster to a cheaper model used about 15% fewer tokens and no drop in scores was seen; three runs cannot rule out a small one, and every other node is untested. Comma-separated node:model pairs; leave blank to use the primary model everywhere. FI does not choose the model for you, and the name must be one your provider's current catalogue actually has: it is passed straight through, not validated.

questions.label: Reasoning effort
questions.prompt: How hard the model reasons before it answers. 'default' sends nothing, so each provider keeps its own default (a local Ollama model then does not think at all). A level is sent as reasoning_effort to HTTP providers (Ollama takes low/medium/high), as --effort to claude_cli and antigravity_cli, and as model_reasoning_effort to codex_cli. copilot_cli, gemini_cli, the VS Code bridge and the proxy providers have no such setting: the level is not sent and the quest log says so once.

choices.label: Provider default (not set)
choices.description: Sends nothing: each provider keeps its own default. A local Ollama model then does not think at all.

choices.label: minimal
choices.description: Not accepted by Ollama, claude_cli or antigravity_cli; skipped there with a warning.

choices.label: low
choices.description: Accepted by every provider FI can set it on.

choices.label: medium
choices.description: Accepted by every provider FI can set it on.

choices.label: high
choices.description: Accepted by every provider FI can set it on.

choices.label: xhigh
choices.description: Not accepted by Ollama or antigravity_cli; skipped there with a warning.

choices.label: max
choices.description: Not accepted by Ollama or antigravity_cli; skipped there with a warning.

questions.label: Custom endpoint (base_url)
questions.prompt: Only for openai/codex/gemini/ollama/vllm: the base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint other than that provider's own default (a self-hosted vLLM server, a corporate gateway, or a third-party model reached the OpenAI-compatible way, such as Moonshot's Kimi at https://api.moonshot.ai/v1). Leave blank to use the provider's own default endpoint.

questions.label: Key environment variable
questions.prompt: Only when the key for the endpoint above is not in that provider's usual variable (OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, ...): the name of the environment variable (or a line in your .env file) FI should read instead. Leave blank to use the provider's own conventional name.

questions.label: Fixed temperature
questions.prompt: Only for a model that answers just one temperature and rejects any other with HTTP 400 (Moonshot's Kimi K2.6 / K3: 0.6 with thinking off, 1 with it on). When set, sent on every call in place of FI's own per-node temperatures. Leave blank to use FI's defaults.

questions.label: Page limit
questions.prompt: The most pages paper.pdf may take, as a whole number. Leave blank (or type none) for no set limit; a limit the topic states, such as '≤ 4 pages', still applies. With a limit the paper gets a tighter layout and the writer a word budget, and each draft is rendered and its pages counted: a draft over the limit is written again, shorter, at most twice.

questions.label: Author (optional)
questions.prompt: Your name as it should appear on the paper, slides and poster. Leave blank to keep the 'Frontier Insight' byline.

questions.label: Affiliation (optional)
questions.prompt: Lab, company or school to print under the author. Leave blank to omit.

questions.label: Contact email (optional)
questions.prompt: Printed on the poster and under the paper title so readers can reach you. It goes only into your own output files. Leave blank to omit.

questions.label: Project link (optional)
questions.prompt: A web page for this work, such as a repository or lab page. The poster prints it as a QR code. Leave blank for no QR code.
